messages:
anya: quick sync — i'm seeing p99 tail spikes on embed/rerank when KV eviction rate climbs. suspecting kernel selection + batching heuristics interacting with eviction churn :thinking_face:
sam: which harness are you using? replay or synth? can you share flags?
anya: replay harness (replay vs synth comparison). command i'm running:```./harness/replay_run --workload s3://bench/replays/2026-03/serve-embed-late-evict.json --model open-embed-1536 --kernels auto --batching dynamic --kv-ttl 120 --collect perf_counters --out s3://artifacts/bench/1945129999/```
perf-bot: job completed — artifact available at https://artifacts.internal/bench/1945129999 (logs + perf counters) :white_check_mark:
dinesh: couple of likely culprits: when sequence len >512 our kernel picker falls back to generic_gemm variant which loses fused-attn optims. that + small inter-request batching (due to eviction delay) can blow p99 by 2-3x.
marie: quick numbers from a short run (vector_dim=1536): replay-auto-kernel -> p50 18ms, p95 76ms, p99 214ms; synth-uniform -> p50 20ms, p95 82ms, p99 128ms. (batch window=10ms). synth seems friendlier to tail because it preserves steady batches.
hao: interesting — is KV hit-rate different between replay and synth? eviction spikes will add prefix decode cost and change seq-len distribution. we should capture per-request kv_hit boolean.
anya: yes, initial dump shows replay has ~14% eviction-triggered misses in tail window vs 2% in synth. added a small probe to log kv_hit distribution.
dinesh: propose experiment matrix: 1) replay + kernels=auto 2) replay + kernels=force-fused 3) synth-steady 4) synth-bursty-with-prefix-reuse. also toggle batching policy to 'eviction-aware' so we don't batch across eviction boundaries.
marie: i pushed a quick script to aggregate traces:```python
# agg example
logs = load_s3('s3://artifacts/bench/1945129999/')
print(quantiles(logs.latency, [50,95,99]))
print(pct(logs.kv_hit, True))
```
sam: how do you enable the eviction-aware batching? is that a config flag or kernel runtime change?
hao: we added an opt in flag in the runtime: `--batch-policy=kv-aware` (it's a heuristic: if a request will trigger eviction within X ms, it preferentially flushes small batches to avoid mixing hot & cold prefixes). can toggle with `--kv-eviction-window-ms` as well.
anya: running the 4x matrix now, each for 15m steady-state. logging perf counters and kernel selection traces (which kernel chosen per request).
perf-bot: run started: job id 1945130102. collecting perf counters, kernel_trace, kv_events. ETA ~45m.
dinesh: reminder: capture GPU kernel names and flop counts (nvtx + host traces). tail spikes often correlate to kernel fallback events, look for `generic_gemm` / `fallback_attn` labels.
marie: preliminary observation from the first 10m of replay+auto: p99 drops from 214ms -> 160ms when `--batch-policy=kv-aware` is enabled. kv_miss rate at tail drops by ~6 percentage points.
anya: nice. also noticed kernel picker sometimes prefers a lower-latency kernel for short seqs even when longer tokens arrive mid-stream — need to re-evaluate decision window.
hao: that suggests we should add a per-batch lookahead: if batch contains mixed seq-len, pick kernel for worst-case to avoid mid-batch fallbacks. but that hurts avg latency.
dinesh: tradeoff. metric to optimize: tail latency at acceptable avg cost. maybe a hybrid: use `force-fused` when more than X% of batch >512, else auto.
marie: i've captured kv_hit heatmap and attached to artifact. heatmap shows bursts where prefixes evict and then multiple subsequent requests pay full decode cost.
anya: next steps: 1) finish matrix and upload artifacts 2) run one canary with `--batch-policy=kv-aware` + hybrid kernel rule 3) write up short methodology note (replay vs synth differences and why we need kv-aware batching)
sam: please add the exact commands in the note and the script to reproduce; i'll run canary in staging after docs.
perf-bot: artifact updated: https://artifacts.internal/bench/1945129999/ (matrix runs, kernel_traces.tar.gz, kv_heatmaps.png)
anya: thanks everyone — i'll open a PR with results + suggested runtime flags and a short appendix on why plain synthetic load underestimates tail risk for eviction-heavy workloads. ping me if you want to be added to the PR reviewers. :rocket:
